The glam booth handles that scale the same way it handles a smaller party: our own studio lighting rig renders every guest's skin tone evenly regardless of how many have come through before them, and unlimited prints and digital copies mean nobody is turned away because the count ran high.

It is also a natural companion to the mirror booth at bigger Staten Island events. When a ballroom's guest list is large enough that one line would run all night, pairing the glam booth with a second station or a roaming attendant keeps both moving — worth mentioning when you request your quote if your Great Kills or St. George venue is expecting a crowd. Todt Hill's more private estate events bring a different flavor: smaller guest lists where the black-and-white look fits a more editorial, considered aesthetic.

Setup wants 10ft x 10ft for the backdrop and prop table, compressing to 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of clearance for tighter halls in New Dorp or Tottenville, plus a standard 110V outlet within 15 feet. Wherever the venue sits on the island, Staten Island is within our standard service area — any bridge toll is built into your quote up front.

faqHeading: Glam Photo Booth on Staten Island — FAQ

faqs.q: Can the glam booth keep up with a large St. George or Great Kills ballroom wedding?
faqs.a: Yes — unlimited sessions and unlimited prints mean guest count isn't a limit. For very large weddings we often suggest pairing the glam booth with a roaming attendant or a second station so the line stays short through cocktail hour.

faqs.q: How much space does the glam booth need at a Staten Island venue?
faqs.a: 10ft x 10ft is optimal for the backdrop, prop table and a red-carpet feel; we can compress to 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of ceiling clearance for tighter rooms.

faqs.q: Is color available, or is it black-and-white only?
faqs.a: Both — the black-and-white glam edit is the signature look, but the booth can output color, black-and-white, or let each guest choose.

faqs.q: What power do you need at a Staten Island venue?
faqs.a: A standard 110V, 5-amp, 3-prong outlet within 15 feet of the booth. Most banquet halls on the island have one available near the reception floor.

faqs.q: Do you charge a travel fee to Staten Island?
faqs.a: No surprise fees beyond the standard bridge toll, which is already built into your quote from your venue's ZIP code.

faqs.q: Is the skin-smoothing retouch too strong, or can we tone it down?
faqs.a: It's fully adjustable — we can push it toward a full editorial look or keep it subtle so guests still look like themselves. Tell us your preference before the event.

faqs.q: Can you send a certificate of insurance for a Staten Island venue that requires one?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million insurance policy — reply to your booking confirmation with the venue's contact and we will send it over.

faqs.q: Is the glam booth a fit for a Todt Hill estate event?
faqs.a: Yes — the black-and-white editorial look works especially well at Todt Hill's more private, design-conscious estate events, where guest lists tend to run smaller and the aesthetic leans considered rather than purely formal.

faqs.q: Would the glam booth work for a Staten Island quinceañera?
faqs.a: Yes. It's a popular choice for the editorial, red-carpet feel that a quinceañera court often wants — the studio lighting flatters the honoree and every generation of guests equally, and prints can be designed around her colors and theme.

faqs.q: Can the glam booth work at a New Dorp or Tottenville backyard celebration, not just a ballroom?
faqs.a: Yes. New Dorp and Tottenville bring us plenty of backyard and small-space bookings, and the glam booth's 8ft x 8ft minimum footprint works fine there — we'll just confirm your power access ahead of time since it's less standardized than a hall's dedicated event floor.
